rule: RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3 / ECMAScript NumberToString: +0 and -0 both become "0"
divergence_trap: Some serializers emit "-0"; plain JSON.stringify(-0) may preserve sign in non-compliant engines

rule: RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3: integers in [-2^53+1, 2^53-1] serialize as decimal without exponent or decimal point
divergence_trap: None for compliant ES6; some libs force scientific notation

rule: RFC 8785 Appendix B table: IEEE 4340000000000000 serializes as 9007199254740992
divergence_trap: Naive big-int path may emit 9007199254740993 or scientific form

rule: RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3 / ES6: magnitude >= 1e21 uses scientific notation with + sign on exponent
divergence_trap: JSON.stringify may omit + ("1e21") or use uppercase E

rule: RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3 / ES6: magnitude < 1e-6 uses scientific notation
RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2: solidus U+002F MUST NOT be escaped (only " and \ and controls)
RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2: U+0000..U+001F must use \u00XX; " and \ must be escaped
divergence_trap: Some libs use \0 or omit leading zeros in \u

rule: RFC 8785 §3.1: no Unicode normalization; preserve code points as-is (composed é stays composed)
divergence_trap: NFC/NFD normalizing implementations rewrite to "e\u0301" or vice-versa

rule: RFC 8785 §3.2.3: keys sorted by UTF-16 code-unit sequences; U+1F600 (D83D DE00) precedes U+FFFD because 0xD83D < 0xFFFD
divergence_trap: Code-point sort (Python sorted, many non-JS) yields {"\uFFFD":1,"\uD83D\uDE00":2}

rule: RFC 8785 §3.2.1 / §3.2.3: empty structures emit {} and []; keys sorted (only one key each here)
divergence_trap: Whitespace-inserting pretty-printers; some emit null for empty
Space-after-colon or trailing commas from non-strict serializers

rule: RFC 8785 §3.1 / I-JSON: objects MUST NOT have duplicate property names; input rejected before canonicalization
divergence_trap: Last-wins parsers silently produce {"a":2}; first-wins produce {"a":1}
